Bialobrzegi New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Białobrzegi, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Białobrzegi developed from the second half of the 18th century; by 1921, 1,418 Jews made up nearly 59% of the town's population, and most were murdered at Treblinka in autumn 1942. This cemetery was likely established around 1861, four years after Białobrzegi's Jews became independent of the Przytyk synagogue supervision they'd previously used for burials. During the war, victims of the Treblinka deportation - roughly 120-200 people - were buried here, before the Germans ordered the bodies exhumed and burned as the cemetery's deliberate destruction began. In 2007, members of a Jewish youth organization collected and reburied scattered bones found on the surface. The Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage fenced the site with concrete in 2015 (funded by Morris and Arlene Goldfarb of New York), adding a commemorative plaque in 2018. Notably, a field survey found no direct evidence confirming this specific plot as the historical cemetery or mass-grave site, despite official records identifying it as such.
